metadata.case_name: FU CHUEN SING v. RYAN (HK) LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: distributor on overnight shift (delivery worker of newspapers and magazines)
plaintiff.occupation_after: salesman for a cable TV company (from 1 September 2008); later salesman for another cable TV company (from 28 October 2009)

injuries.description: lower back pain / sprained his back
source: diagnosis is lower back pain post injury
Back injury resulting in persistent back pain
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: tenderness over lower lumbar spine / minimal tenderness at the left paraspinal area
range of movement of lumbosacral spine full but mildly limited by pain; extension of the back was limited; forward flexion limited (to knee level / to both shins)
difficulty walking up and down stairs
unable to bend his back below 90 degrees
unable to stand for more than 1-2 hours; unable to sit for more than 30 minutes
sexual activity affected by back pain
unable to participate in sports activities such as playing basketball, swimming and running
walking and sitting were not limited at final assessment but pain over left side of lower back remained (70% improvement noted)

source: The Plaintiff was given analgesics and sick leave.
The Plaintiff was given analgesics and sick leave.
The Plaintiff produced sick leave certificates for 2 days (13-14 March 2008) given by private doctor Dr. Chan Ching Sou and for around 5 months given by public clinics (28 March – 10 September 2008).
The sick leave period certified by Employees’ Compensation (Ordinary Assessment) Board was for a total of 218 days (intermittent during the period from 13 March 2008 to 4 November 2008).

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (28 sessions including shortware diathermy, mobilization and strengthening exercises and condition training)
source: The Plaintiff was also given 28 sessions at Physiotherapy Department of TMH which included shortware diathermy, mobilization and strengthening exercises and condition training.
According to the Physiotherapy Report, on final clinical assessment before discharge on 8 August 2008, Plaintiff had 70% improvement.

treatments_received.treatment: occupational therapy (2 sessions) and discharge with home program and stretching exercise
source: He was further given 1 work assessment session and 2 sessions for occupational therapy and then discharged with home program and stretching exercise taught.

treatments_received.treatment: out-patient follow-up sessions (5 sessions at YFSHC, 46 sessions at YLJCHC, 2 sessions at TMC, 1 session at TMH and 1 session at POH)
source: He attended 5 sessions at YFSHC, 46 sessions at YLJCHC, 2 sessions at TMC, 1 session at TMH and 1 session at POH for out-patient follow-up.

treatments_received.treatment: advice: resume modified duty but avoid lifting heavy objects
source: Physiotherapy Department of TMH suggested that Plaintiff could resume modified duty but avoid lifting heavy objects.
He was further given 1 work assessment session and 2 sessions for occupational therapy and then discharged with home program and stretching exercise taught.

losses.description: back pain when walking up and down stairs; unable to stand for more than 1-2 hours; unable to sit for more than 30 minutes; unable to bend his back below 90 degrees

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: unable to participate in sports activities such as playing basketball, swimming and running

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: sexual activity affected by back pain
